rv.q: This musical will not change your brain in any way, but it delivers what it promises: a big Broadway production that leaves you grinning, and a star performer with the poise, charm and chops to make you believe that what the world needs now might be, of all things, a little more Betty Boop.
Thus “Boop!” builds and communicates its own optimistic world, inhabits it fully and makes no apology to anyone.
Whatever you may feel about the big-eyed flapper, the attraction today is not the ​t​itle, but Rogers​.
"Boop!" shows that cartoon makeovers may be an enticing novelty, but to really succeed it first needs to be well drawn.
The thing adds up to less than the sum of its bits.
Never mind that Monroe was more siren than foghorn; their resounding pipes are the highlight of an otherwise thinly conceived spin-off.
Instead, one feels at all times the heavy hooves of a marketing imperative.
Yet you will likely have more fun at Boop! than in many other theaters this spring.
Hurtling towards us through metaphysical universes and a sometimes bumpy production, Rogers arrives fully-formed: a star.

With a zippy score, terrific tap numbers choreographed by director Jerry Mitchell, energetic performances from a top-notch cast, and a plot that doesn’t tax your brain, Boop! is one of the feel-good musicals of the year.
Maybe it’s Betty’s unshakeable optimism rubbing off, but Boop!, for all its unmissably ramshackle flaws, is joyously irresistible.
Little of it feels original, and none of it feels necessary.
Even so, the entire evening is lots of fun.

Yet all this effort is in service of one of the most maladroit storylines Broadway has encountered in years, with cardboard characters that serve plot purposes only, a book that doesn’t listen to the lyrics and dialogue that doesn’t listen to itself.
Betty Boop may be ready for her close-up, but this isn’t the vehicle she deserves.
Playing that creep, Erich Bergen singlehandedly turns “Boop!” into something worth watching after nearly two hours of total tedium.
“Boop” is one of those old fashioned, heartfelt, feel-good musicals that helps shed just a bit more radiance on an already brightly lit Great White Way!
Whether in trousers or a skirt, she show’s enough versatility to cement her status as a major new Broadway talent.
But most people will have a better time just joining in the merriment.
Boop! is one musical that earns its exclamation point.

Still, for the most part, “Boop!” too rarely rises above the level of pleasant fluff during its two-and-half-hours, which can be frustrating since the show’s potential for greatness is obviously within reach.
It seems that Boop! The Musical has a new star rather than an old one.
